citations.quote: When the binomial tree is used to price a European option, the price converges to the Black–Scholes–Merton price, as expected, as the number of time steps is increased.
This model with two possible outcomes is called the binomial model.

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: The binomial tree replaces continuous geometric Brownian motion with a discrete two-state lattice. Backward induction discounts risk-neutral expected child values with q = (e^{r·dt} - d) / (u - d). The CRR parameterization u = exp(σ·√dt) makes the lattice price converge to BSM; American options use max(intrinsic, continuation) at each node.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Binomial-Tree Option Valuation
